conclusion.what_it_buys: A balanced common-seed design removes the confounding between the environment term and the seeds a stack happens to have: with 4 seeds on all 4 stacks at rank 5 the between-environment and within-environment sums of squares are no longer driven by which stack has more seeds, and the environment share is estimated from matched seed sets (the seed set common to every populated stack today is 42,123,999). 2/4 stacks currently carry all 4 common seeds; after the plan the environment share is 0.531 with CI95 [0.202, 0.890] (width 0.689) against 0.443 with CI95 [0.189, 0.747] (width 0.557) today, and sigma_env is 35.1 against 31.8.
caveats: the rank-6 side of the design is planned and priced the same way; S37's headline decomposition is the rank-5 one

the torch26 rows are produced by the training script and only become stack-tagged rows after the runner copies them to the _torch26 name; run_training.py overwrites the untagged name, which belongs to another stack's archived row, so that name must be preserved (the runner saves and restores it)
a common-seed design does not remove the hardware mixing inside the torch26 stack (seed 42 on the workstation, seeds 7/123/999 on the cloud GPU), which the S29 machine column must state
the per-run wall clock of the torch24 and cloud stacks is not recorded by any archive of this protocol, so their share of the GPU-hour estimate is stated as unknown
